extra_prompt: You are booking for a heating and cooling company. Ask the brand and model if known, the system type (split, ducted, evaporative, heat pump, or gas heater), and its approximate age. Ask whether the unit runs at all and whether it blows warm or cold air. For gas heaters, a gas smell, a yellow or orange flame, or a carbon monoxide alarm is an emergency: tell the caller to turn the heater off, open windows, and get everyone outside, then treat it as an emergency. For installs, offer an on-site assessment before quoting.

kb.q: Do you do emergency AC repair?
kb.a: Yes, we run an emergency line for no-cooling and no-heating calls. Availability depends on the season and how busy we are.

kb.q: Do you install new systems?
kb.a: Yes, we install and replace split systems, ducted systems, and heat pumps. We do a load calculation and a commissioning check on every install.

kb.q: How much does a new AC unit cost?
kb.a: {price_note} Costs depend on the system type, the size needed, and how complex the install is. We give you a fixed quote after a site visit.

kb.q: Do you service commercial HVAC?
kb.a: Yes, we service light commercial systems, including rooftop units and split systems. Commercial jobs are quoted after a site visit.

kb.q: What brands do you work on?
kb.a: We work on [list of brands you service]. Tell us your brand and model when you book, so we bring the right parts.

kb.q: How long does a service call take?
kb.a: A standard AC service usually takes [number] hours. Diagnosis can take longer if the fault is complex.

kb.q: Do you offer financing?
kb.a: If financing is available, we explain the options when we quote. [financing provider, or state that financing is not offered].

kb.q: Why is my AC leaking water?
kb.a: Usually a blocked condensate drain. It is a common problem, and we can often clear it in a single visit.

kb.q: My system is frozen. What should I do?
kb.a: Turn the system off at the thermostat straight away. Running a frozen system can damage the compressor. Then call us so we can diagnose the cause.

kb.q: How often should I change my filter?
kb.a: Standard filters usually need changing every one to three months. High-efficiency or heavily used systems may need more frequent changes.

kb.q: Do you provide a warranty on repairs?
kb.a: {warranty_note} Ask us to explain what is covered before the job starts.

kb.q: Can you install a smart thermostat?
kb.a: Yes, we install and set up smart thermostats. Tell us the model you want, and we will confirm it works with your system.

kb.q: Do you test for carbon monoxide?
kb.a: Yes, our gas heater service includes a carbon monoxide safety check. If you think there is carbon monoxide now, leave the property and call emergency services.

kb.q: How long does a new system install take?
kb.a: Most residential replacements take about a day. Ducted or commercial systems can take longer, and we confirm the timing when we quote.

kb.q: Do you offer maintenance plans?
kb.a: Yes, we offer an annual maintenance plan. Ask us what is included, such as the number of services and booking priority, before you sign up.

kb.q: What energy rating should my new system have?
kb.a: A higher energy rating usually means lower running costs but a higher upfront cost. We help match the rating to your climate and how you use the system.

kb.q: Can you repair a unit over twenty years old?
kb.a: We can, but on very old equipment we weigh the repair cost against replacement and give you both options.

kb.q: How often should I service my air conditioner?
kb.a: Most systems need a service once a year, ideally before summer or winter. Regular service keeps the efficiency up and helps prevent breakdowns.

kb.q: Is it worth repairing an old system?
kb.a: A repair is often worth it on a system under about ten years old. For older systems, we give you the repair cost and the replacement cost so you can decide.

kb.q: Why does my air conditioner smell musty?
kb.a: A musty smell is usually mould or bacteria on the evaporator coil or in the drain pan. A clean and sanitise fixes most cases.

kb.q: Why is water dripping inside from my indoor unit?
kb.a: The condensate drain is usually blocked, or the unit is not level. Switch the unit off and book a service so the drain can be cleared and checked.

kb.q: What size system do I need?
kb.a: It depends on room size, insulation, sun exposure, and ceiling height. We do a load calculation on site and recommend a size that suits the space.

compliance.guidance: Confirm the licence class and registration that cover this work before you quote, and show the licence number where your state requires it. Some work (for example gas, electrical and some plumbing or roofing) must be signed off by a licensed person. Your state regulator sets the rules; check them before relying on this guidance.
